candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — safe medication administration and use of technology
candidate.educational_objective: Explain how BCMA supports point-of-care medication verification and error prevention.

options.A: Replace nursing judgment and all independent safety checks.
options.B: Electronically verify the medication and patient at the point of administration and link the administration to the medication record.
options.C: Limit medication verification to controlled substances only.
options.D: Serve mainly as a billing tool rather than an error-prevention system.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ describes BCMA as a point-of-care safety technology that scans medication and patient identifiers to verify the right medication for the right patient and links administration to the electronic medication record. BCMA can reduce administration errors but does not replace clinical judgment. Therefore B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: BCMA uses barcode labeling of patients, medications, and records to electronically link the correct dose/medication to the correct patient and reduce medication-administration errors.
candidate.source_locator: High Tech Solutions — Barcode medication administration
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) PSNet
candidate.stem: What is the primary medication-safety function of barcode medication administration (BCMA)?
